items.title: 중국, 한화오션 미국 관련 자회사 5곳 제재 유예 2개월 연장

items.snippet: 도레이첨단소재는 9일부터 1박2일 일정으로 제5포병여단 모범 간부 부부 12쌍을 초청해 교류 행사를 열었다고 밝혔다.참가자들은 첫날 서울 마곡 한국도레이 연구개발(R&D)센터를 방문해 회사 현황을 살펴본 뒤 경복궁을 견학하고 환영행사에 참석했다. 둘째 날에는 인천 차이나타운을 방문할 예정이다.도레이첨단소재는 2012년 제5포병여단과 자매결연을 맺은 이후 발전기금 전달과 임직원 자녀 병영체험, 모범 간부 초청 행사 등을 이어오고 있다.김영섭 도레이첨단소재 사장은 "국민의 안전과 국가 안보를 위해 헌신하는 장병 여러분께 깊이 감사드린다

items.title: 서경배 아모레 회장에 주식 증여받은 친인척 2명, 일부 매도
items.snippet: 서경배 아모레퍼시픽그룹 회장에게 아모레퍼시픽 주식을 증여받은 친인척 5명 중 2명이 지분 일부를 매도했다.9일 금융감독원 전자공시시스템에 따르면 서 회장과 친인척인 서인선, 서주현 씨는 지난 달 장내매도로 각각 아모레퍼시픽[090430] 지분 5천500주, 500주를 팔았다.매도 전일 주가를 기준으로 하면 각각 7억3천만 원, 7천만 원어치다.매도 이후 서인선 씨는 1천989주, 서주현 씨는 3천207주를 보유하게 된다.앞서 서 회장은 지난 달 20일 친인척 5명에게 아모레퍼시픽 주식 45억 원어치를 증여했다. 당시 서인선 씨와

items.title: 글로벌테크놀로지, 중국서 디스플레이 기술 심포지엄 개최
items.snippet: 글로벌테크놀로지가 중국 선전에서 현지 디스플레이 업체와 산업 파트너를 대상으로 기술 심포지엄을 열었다. 시분할 구동(TSO) 기술과 IC, 광학, 패키지를 결합한 솔루션을 소개하고 제품 적용과 생산·판매 협력 방안을 논의했다.글로벌테크놀로지는 최근 중국 선전에서 'GT 테크 심포지엄 2026'을 개최했다고 9일 밝혔다. 행사에는 TCL CSOT와 이노룩스, ZTE, WG 테크, 네이션스타 등 디스플레이·반도체 관련 업체들이 참석했다.TSO는 하나의 발광다이오드(LED) 구동 채널을 시간차로 나눠 여러 LED를 구동하는 기술이다. 구

items.title: 한화세미텍, 컨설팅 전문가 김진우 사업총괄 신임 대표로 내정
items.snippet: 한화세미텍이 회계와 컨설팅 전문가 김진우 사업총괄을 신임 대표로 내정했다고 9일 밝혔다. 기술 전문가 대신 경영 전문가를 전면에 내세워 사업 경쟁력을 강화한다.김 신임 대표 내정자는 고대역폭메모리(HBM) 핵심인 열압착(TC)본더, 하이브리드본더, 패널레벨페키징(PLP) 등 반도체 후공정 장비 시장에 집중한다. 한화세미텍은 "회사의 성장에 한층 속도가 붙을 것"이라고 기대했다. 김 신임 대표 내정자는 고려대학교 통계학과를 출신이다. 반도체와 이차전지, 산업기계 분야에서 사업전략 수립과 추진에 기여해 왔다. KPMG, AT Kearn

items.title: SKT·엔비디아·리벨리온, 한국형 소버린 AI 구축 '삼각편대'

items.title: 두산, 3Q 연결 영업익 두배 뛴 4천600억…기대치 부합
items.snippet: 두산[000150]의 3분기 연결 엉업익이 전년 동기보다 두배 가까이 상승하며 시장의 기대치에 부합했다.두산은 9일 3분기 연결 실적을 잠정 집계한 결과 매출액은 5조4천269억원으로 전년동기보다 22.2% 증가했다고 공시했다. 영업이익은 4천594억원으로 같은 기간 98.4% 뛰었다.매출액과 영업이익 모두 시장 기대치에 부합했다.연합인포맥스가 지난 1개월간 주요 증권사 3곳이 제출한 실적 전망치를 분석한 결과 두산의 3분기 매출액은 5조3천924억원(21.11%), 영업이익은 4천707억원(103.5%) 상승할 것으로 전망됐다.

items.title: 쿠팡, 예상보다 7배 커진 과징금에 반발…배민도 "위법성 없다"

items.title: 배터리·타이어 동반 부진에…한국앤컴퍼니, 3Q 영업익 전년비 52% 급감

items.snippet: 이용철 법무부 장관 후보자가 8일 이재명 대통령 관련 사건에 대한 공소취소 논란과 관련해 “좀 정리해서 말씀드릴 생각”이라고 밝혔다. 전임 정성호 장관이 “불법적 절차로 기소됐다면 검찰(현 공소청)이 판단해야 할 문제”라며 법무부 장관의 공소취소 권한에 대해 선을 그은 바 있다. 6일 국회 본회의를 통과해 국무회의 의결을 앞둔 ‘조작수사·조작기소 진상규명 특검법’(조작기소 특검법)을 둘러싼 논란에는 “앞서 ‘선관위 특검법’도 여야가 (특검 파견 검사에 대한 수사권 부여에) 합의했는데, 왜 이 건에만 위헌을 얘기하나”라고 반박했다. ‘대장동의 숨은 설계자’라는 야권 공세에는 “대장동 사업에 대해서 아는 게 거의 없다”고 일축했다.● 이용철 “李와 굉장히 조심스럽게 친해” 이 후보자는 8일 동아일보와의 통화에서 이 대통령이 자신을 지명한 게 공소...

items.title: 靑, ‘조작기소 특검법 위헌소지 없다’ 판단… 380억 투입될듯
items.snippet: ‘조작수사·조작기소 진상규명 특검법’(조작기소 특검법)에 대해 여권 내부에서도 위헌 우려가 나오는 것과 관련해 청와대는 “법리적 문제가 없다”는 입장인 것으로 알려졌다. 정부는 이르면 17일 이재명 대통령 주재 국무회의에 조작기소 특검법을 상정해 의결할 것으로 보인다. 조작기소 특검에는 이재명 정부 들어 출범한 7번의 특검 중 가장 많은 380억5600만 원이 투입될 것으로 계산됐다. 여권 핵심 관계자는 8일 통화에서 “청와대는 조작기소 특검법이 위헌 소지가 없다고 판단했다”며 “법리적 검토를 끝낸 법안인데 우려할 것이 있느냐”고 말했다. 이어 더불어민주당 내부에서 나온 위헌 소지 등의 지적에 대해서도 “청와대는 소수 의견으로 보고 있다”고 했다. 정부 관계자는 “11일경 정부로 법안이 이송되면 법무부 등 소관 부처 검토를 거쳐 상정될 것”이...

items.title: 李 “정치인 칭찬하되 숭배말라” 또 강경파 직격
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 8일 “칭찬하되 찬양하지 말고, 지지하되 숭배하지 말라”고 밝혔다. 구체적인 대상을 지목하진 않았지만 이른바 ‘무극파’(무책임한 극단주의파)를 재차 겨냥했다는 해석이 나온다. 이 대통령은 이날 0시 30분경 X(옛 트위터)에 “정치인이나 지도적 인사들에게는 칭찬도 지지도 필요하지만, 그것이 종교적 찬양이나 숭배에 이르러서는 안 된다”며 이같이 말했다. 이어 “민주주의는 저절로 오지도 않고 저절로 지켜지지도 않는다”며 “살아 있는 이성으로 진실과 정의에 반응하는 시민들의 끊임없는 참여와 실천만이 민주주의를 만들고 지킨다”고 했다. 그러면서 “행동하지 않는 양심은 악의 편이라며 할 수 있는 게 없다면 담벼락에 고함이라도 지르라시던 김대중 대통령님 말씀이 떠오른다”며 “노무현 대통령께서도 깨어 있는 시민의 조직된 힘을 강조하셨다....

items.snippet: 북한 내 중국통으로 꼽히는 김성남 노동당 국제비서 겸 국제부장이 닷새간의 방중을 통해 중국 최고위급 인사들과 잇달아 회동한 뒤 귀국했다. 김성남이 카운터파트인 류하이싱(劉海星) 중국 공산당 대외연락부장은 물론이고 중국 권력 서열 5위인 차이치(蔡奇) 중국 중앙정치국 상무위원과 중국 외교정책을 총괄하는 왕이(王毅) 외교부장을 두루 만난 것. 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령이 참석 의사를 밝힌 18일 중국 선전 아시아태평양경제협력체(APEC) 정상회의를 열흘가량 앞둔 이번 방중을 두고 일각에선 김정은 북한 국무위원장의 방중과 시진핑(習近平) 중국 국가주석과의 회담을 사전 조율했을 가능성이 제기된다. 중간선거 참패로 트럼프 대통령이 김 위원장과의 대화 재개 등 외교 성과에 매달릴 것이라는 전망이 나오는 가운데 북한이 미국과의 대화를 염두에 두고 중국을...

items.snippet: 정부가 서울 용산공원 내 주택 공급을 위해 옛 방위사업청과 군인아파트, 장교숙소 5단지 등 3곳을 우선 검토 대상으로 추린 것으로 확인됐다. 이미 개발돼 있어 녹지 훼손 우려가 적은 공원 외곽부터 공급 가능성을 살펴보겠다는 취지다. 다만 이를 위해서는 법 개정이 필요하고 서울시 등 지방자치단체의 반대도 넘어야 한다. 8일 국토교통부에 따르면 국토부는 9월 말 국무회의에서 이 같은 내용의 ‘용산 미군 반환부지 추진현황’을 보고했다. 보고 자료에는 공원 북쪽의 옛 방사청(9만6000㎡)과 군인아파트(4만8000㎡), 남동쪽의 장교숙소 5단지(5만2000㎡) 등 총 19만6000㎡ 규모를 우선 검토한다는 내용이 담겼다. 용산공원 본체 부지(약 300만 ㎡)의 6.5% 수준이다. 국토부는 이들 부지가 이미 주거·업무시설로 사용된 데다 공원 외곽에 있...

items.snippet: 위험물 안전점검이나 방재훈련 등 위험한 업무를 수행하다 순직한 일반직 공무원이 별도의 보훈심사 없이 국가유공자로 등록될 수 있도록 제도 개선이 추진된다. 인사혁신처에서 ‘위험직무순직’을 인정받고도 국가보훈부에서 다시 심사를 받아야 하는 중복 절차를 없애기로 한 것이다. 국가보훈부는 8일 이 같은 내용을 담은 ‘국가유공자 등 예우 및 지원에 관한 법률 시행령’ 개정안을 입법 예고했다고 밝혔다. 기존에는 일반직 공무원이 인사혁신처에서 위험직무순직 인정을 받아도 국가유공자로 등록되려면 보훈부 보훈심사위원회의 심의·의결을 다시 거쳐야 했다. 개정안이 시행되면 인사혁신처의 인정 결과에 따라 별도 보훈심사 없이 ‘순직공무원’으로 국가유공자 등록을 할 수 있게 된다. 순직공무원은 군인·경찰·소방공무원을 제외한 공무원 가운데 국민 보호 직무 중 사망한 사람...

items.title: 낚싯대 챔질할 때 동사는 pull? set? reel?
items.snippet: 뉴질랜드 북섬의 베이오브아일랜즈(Bay of Islands) 앞바다로 보트 낚시 투어를 나왔습니다. 난생처음 도전해 보는 바다 낚시입니다. 낚싯줄을 드리우고 설레는 마음으로 기다리는데, 갑자기 손끝에 톡톡 전해지는 미세한 진동이 느껴지며 낚싯대 끝 초릿대가 파르르 떨립니다. ‘지금 당장 낚싯대를 위로 팍 채야 하나? 아니면 물고기가 바늘을 완전히 삼켜 묵직해질 때까지 기다려야 하나?’ 심장은 쿵쾅거리는데 타이밍을 도무지 알 수가 없습니다. 옆의 노련한 현지 선원에게 “톡톡 건드리는 입질이 오는데, 정확히 언제 낚아채야 하나요?”라고 다급히 물으려는데 “When fish eat, when pull?” “Fish touch, upper power?” 같은 엉성한 표현만 입안을 맴돕니다.

items.snippet: 지난 6일 더불어민주당이 강행 처리한 ‘조작기소 특검법’이 시행되면 이재명 대통령이 임명한 특검은 준비 기간 20일을 포함해 최장 200일 동안 수사한다. 이번 특검은 과거 검찰이 수사하고 기소한 사건 17건과 관련해 검사들의 불법 행위가 있었는지 수사한다. 수사 대상 중 이 대통령 관련 사건이 8건, 문재인 정부 관련 사건이 6건이다. 법조계에선 “‘검찰개혁’을 명분으로 검사의 수사권을 완전 폐지한 정부·여당이 이제는 과거 자기들을 수사한 전·현직 검사들에 대한 보복에 나서려는 것 아니냐”는 말이 나온다.

items.title: “운동으로 암 이기자”… 암 환자들, 가족·의사와 함께 달렸다
items.snippet: 7일 오전 10시 서울 서대문구 연세대 신촌캠퍼스 대운동장. 파란 티셔츠를 입은 참가자들이 “운동이 암을 이긴다”고 외치며 달려나갔다. 털모자를 쓴 암 환자와 가족들은 손을 맞잡고 “할 수 있다” “끝까지 가보자”며 발을 내디뎠다. 연세암병원과 연세대, 서울 서대문구청이 암을 예방하고 암 환자 건강 증진을 위해 공동 개최한 ‘제2회 온코런(OncoRun)’ 마라톤이다. 이날 행사는 연세대 대운동장을 출발해 안산 자락길로 이어지는 5㎞ 달리기와 캠퍼스 안을 도는 3㎞ 걷기 코스로 나눠 진행했다. 암 환자와 암 완치자, 지역 주민 등 1100여 명이 참가했다.

items.title: Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits
items.abstract: Logical qubits encoded in collective states of multiple spins are promising building blocks for large-scale semiconductor quantum processors. As novel fault-tolerant architectures increasingly rely on qubit shuttling, understanding decoherence of the shuttled multi-spin qubits becomes crucial. We analyze fidelity and leakage of the logical qubits dephased by the spatio-temporally correlated $1/f$ noise, considering two-, three-, and four-spin encodings. We study different shuttling protocols and establish that for all encodings generally, parallel shuttling provides the best protection against decoherence at short distances, whereas sequential shuttling outperforms others for long-range transport (although the exact boundaries depend on the specific device parameters). items.title: Discrete time crystals and heteroclinic switching in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers
items.abstract: We investigate the mechanisms underlying the emergence of discrete time crystals in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers. Our analysis is based on a Haus master equation generalized to retain carrier memory between round-trips. We perform a detailed bifurcation analysis that reveals a well-defined hierarchy of subharmonic states, illustrating how pulses may suppress their neighbors when the modulation runs faster than the pulse round-trip frequency. To identify the underlying mechanism, we derive effective equations of motion that couple the pulse energies, their positions relative to the modulation transmission maxima, and the local time-dependent gain. These reveal that transitions between time-crystalline states occur via transcritical global bifurcations, opening a regime of heteroclinic winnerless competition between symmetry-degenerate configurations.

items.title: Microscopic theory of exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides
items.abstract: Polarons are composite quasiparticles formed when charge carriers strongly couple to lattice vibrations, manifesting as carriers dressed by a surrounding cloud of phonons. Although this dressing fundamentally renormalizes the effective mass and mobility of carriers, its impact on electrically neutral exciton polarons in 2D semiconductors has received limited attention. In particular, despite the growing interest in polaronic effects in atomically thin semiconductors, only a few theoretical studies have addressed spectral signatures and renormalized properties of exciton polarons in these materials. Here, we develop a microscopic model to describe exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides. items.title: Exciton design via topological spin textures
items.abstract: Excitons carry energy and information through a semiconductor without carrying charge. This makes them attractive for optoelectronics, but also hard to guide. Magnetic skyrmions, on the other hand, are moved by small electrical currents. Here we develop a theory of excitons interacting with a skyrmion in which the electron and the hole are treated as distinct constituents, each with its own spin--orbit coupling. We find that the topology of the skyrmion is transferred to the exciton only when the exchange coupling exceeds the relevant spin--orbit splitting. The exciton then experiences a full flux quantum, with opposite signs in the two valleys. The quantum metric of the spin texture creates a ring-shaped barrier that traps excitons, whereas the topological charge fixes the angular momentum of the trapped states and hence their optical selection rules. items.abstract: High-precision astrometry is a cornerstone for detecting Earth-like exoplanets in the habitable zones of nearby solar-type stars and probing the nature of dark matter in galactic environments. This paper reviews recent progress in characterizing large format detector at the micropixel scale level, calibrating optical distortion using reference stars, and refining differential astrometry methods to detect the faint astrometric signatures of Earth-mass exoplanets. We highlight the latest developments in the RETINA project, which aims to advance the TRL of GIGAPYX 220 MP CMOS detectors from Pyxalis which are critical components for future space missions such as ESA's Theia and NASA's Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). items.title: On the collective flow puzzle in ultra-central heavy-ion collisions
items.abstract: Using UCC-DiffHIC, an AI-accelerated event-by-event hydrodynamic model validated against hybrid simula- tions, we study flow in ultracentral Pb-Pb collisions. For suitable initial conditions, the calculated v2{2}/v3{2} approaches unity in the most central collisions, consistent with experiment. An exact response decomposition shows that residual fluctuations suppress the ratio through P3/P2 < 1, where P2 and P3 are Pearson response correlations for elliptic and triangular flow, respectively. This resolves the apparent flow hierarchy without requiring a breakdown of linear response or additional effects such as nuclear deformation.

items.snippet: 더불어민주당 주도로 6일 국회 본회의를 통과한 ‘조작기소 특검법’에는 위헌·위법 소지가 있는 독소 조항이 여럿 담겨 논란이 일고 있다. 이번 특검법 수사 대상에는 대장동 개발 비리, 쌍방울 불법 대북 송금 사건 등 이재명 대통령이 기소돼 재판이 중단된 사건 8건이 포함돼 있고, 특검은 과거 검찰이 이 사건들을 수사하는 과정에서 위법이 있었는지 수사하게 된다. 법조계에선 “형사 사법 제도의 사유화” “대통령을 위해 법 질서를 무너뜨리겠다는 것”이라는 비판이 나왔다.

items.title: 대구 달성군 출생아 수, 전국 82개 군 중에서 10년 연속 1위
items.snippet: 지난해 대구 달성군에서 태어난 아이는 1508명으로 전국 82개 군(郡) 가운데 가장 많았다. 2016년부터 10년 연속 1위다. 올해 1~9월 출생아도 1265명으로 지난해 같은 기간(1132명)보다 133명(11.7%) 늘었다. 지난해 합계출산율(여성 1명이 평생 낳을 것으로 예상되는 평균 출생아 수)은 1.02명으로 전국 평균(0.8명)을 웃돌았다. 달성군은 일자리, 주거, 보육 삼박자를 갖춘 곳이다. 달성군 현풍읍과 유가읍에는 첨단산업도시 대구테크노폴리스가 조성됐다. HD현대로보틱스 등 기업과 대구경북과학기술원(DGIST)이 들어서 있다. 근처에는 대구국가산업단지도 있다. 일자리가 생기고 아파트 단지가 들어서면서 젊은 부부가 모여들었다. 달성군 인구는 1995년 대구시 편입 당시 11만3000명에서 지난해 26만3000명으로 두 배 넘...

items.title: “결혼 6년 만에 낳은 아이, 최고의 피로회복제”
items.snippet: “집돌이·집순이였던 저희 부부는 두 딸이 태어난 뒤 대구 명소를 찾아 산책하는 게 취미가 됐습니다. 일이 바빠 두 딸 모두 돌잔치를 못 해줬는데, 오늘이 우리 가족 최고의 돌잔치 날이네요.”(‘31초 우리가족 행복담기 영상제’ 대상 김태형씨)

items.title: 선생님 부담 줄이려다…원장들은 ‘0세반 기피’
items.snippet: 정부가 어린이집 0세반 교사 1명당 아동 수를 3명에서 2명으로 줄이는 정책을 추진 중인 가운데, 이를 따르면 한 반당 보육료 수입이 매달 60만원가량 줄어드는 것으로 나타났다. 수요 증가에도 운영할수록 손해가 예상되는 구조 탓에 원장들이 0세반을 기피하는 현상까지 나타나고 있다.

items.title: 12월 법관회의, 이달 30일로 앞당겨… 대법원장 국조·탄핵 대응 방안 논의
items.snippet: 판사 회의체인 전국법관대표회의가 오는 30일 정기회의를 연다. 원래 다음 달 7일 열 예정이던 회의를 앞당긴 것이다. 여권이 조희대 대법원장에 대한 국회 국정조사 등 사법부 압박에 나서자, 판사들이 대응 방안을 논의하자고 요구한 데 따른 것이다. 법관대표회의는 6일 “정기회의를 앞당기는 방안에 대한 투표를 진행한 결과 2026년 하반기 정기회의 개최일을 이달 30일로 변경하기로 했다”고 밝혔다. 투표는 지난 4일 진행됐다.

items.title: 공소청, 강호동 농협중앙회장 구속영장 기각
items.snippet: 서울중앙지방공소청이 6일 경찰이 신청했던 강호동 농협중앙회장에 대한 구속영장을 기각했다.

items.title: 입동 하루 앞두고 기온 뚝
items.snippet: 6일 서울 종로구 경복궁에서 관광객들이 두꺼운 외투에 목도리를 한 차림으로 길을 걷고 있다. 절기상 입동(立冬)인 7일에는 찬 북서풍의 영향으로 전국의 기온이 크게 떨어질 전망이다. 7일 전국 최저기온은 영하 6도에서 영상 5도로 예상된다. 서울도 7일 최저기온이 영하 1도까지 내려가, 일부 지역에는 살얼음이 얼 수 있다. 입동에 서울 최저기온이 5도 밑으로 내려간 건 최근 10년간 세 차례에 불과했다. 작년 입동에는 최저 8.3도, 최고 19.9도로 포근했다.

items.title: “월세 부담 덜고 생활비 아끼고” 동거커플 31% 증가
items.snippet: 서울 마포구에 사는 나모(30)씨는 6년 전 취업에 성공했다. 나씨는 회사에 다니며 월급을 받기 시작했지만 월세와 생활비를 내고 나면 통장에 남는 돈은 얼마 되지 않았다고 한다. 나씨는 내 집 마련은커녕 결혼 자금을 모으기도 막막했다. 비슷한 시기에 취업한 여자 친구도 같은 고민을 하고 있었다.

items.title: 눈도 안 마주치던 다문화 아이들… 함께 축구공 차니 어느새 ‘한 팀’
items.snippet: “처음에는 러시아와 우크라이나 출신 아이들끼리 서로 패스조차 하지 않았어요. 그런데 넉 달 동안 함께 뛰고 땀 흘리다 보니 어느새 한 팀이 되더라고요.”

items.title: 엄우종 세계은행 부총재
items.snippet: 세계은행그룹(WBG)이 신설한 독립책임성기구 부총재에 엄우종 전 아시아개발은행(ADB) 사무총장이 선임됐다고 6일 재정경제부가 밝혔다. 그는 앞으로 세계은행 사업 관련 분쟁해결, 규정 준수 검토 및 자문 기능을 총괄하게 된다. 한국인이 세계은행그룹 부총재에 오른 것은 2024년 7월 김상부 디지털·인공지능 부총재에 이어 두 번째다.

items.title: 백현주한복연구소, 동티모르 대통령에 한복 선물
items.snippet: 백현주(오른쪽) 백현주한복연구소 대표가 지난 15일 서울 신라호텔에서 한국을 공식 방문한 조제 하무스 오르타 동티모르 대통령에게 전통 한복을 선물했다. 연구소는 1996년 노벨평화상 수상자인 오르타 대통령에게 한복을 선물하며 우리 민족의 아름다운 복식 문화와 전통의 가치를 전했다고 밝혔다. /백현주한복연구소

items.snippet: ▲행정안전부◇실장급 전보▷안전예방정책실장 박천수▷사회재난실장 박형배◇과장급 전보▷안전소통담당관 김재웅▷교부세과장 신일철▷안전사업조정과장 류성수▷자연재난대응과장 이일령▷상황담당관 김미순▷기후재난관리과장 장형석▷보건사회재난대응과장 이상목▷민방위과장 김정훈

items.title: [부음] 김시대 별세 외
items.snippet: ▲ 김시대 별세, 서영숙 남편상, 김효정 주간조선 취재2팀장· 김종극 진량고 교육과정부장 부친상, 홍성윤 매일경제신문 기자 장인상, 윤미정 대구신용보증재단 근무 시부상=5일21시54분 경북 안동병원, 발인 7일6시, (054)840-0030 ▲ 김용무 별세, 김재형 서울대 법학전문대학원 교수· 김세영 부친상, 전현정 · 선순주 시부상=6일8시35분 서울대병원, 발인 8일7시, (02)2072-2014

items.title: [오늘의 날씨] 2026년 11월 7일
실패에 관대하지 못한 사회엔 희망이 없다
items.snippet: 2008년 미국발 금융위기 당시 그 충격은 단순히 미국뿐 아니라 전 세계 다른 국가들에도 영향을 주었다. 그 국가들 중 하나가 미국과 특히 친밀한 관계에 있었던 영국이었다. 하지만 2008~2010년 미국에서 도산한 은행이 300개가 넘었던 반면, 영국에서 같은 시기 도산한 은행은 5개에 불과했다. 이 숫자만 보면 금융기관의 위험한 투자 행위를 방관했던 미국 정부와 비교해서 금융기관에 대한 감독과 규제를 게을리하지 않은 영국 정부의 정책이 옳았다고 생각하기 쉽다.

items.title: 실록 지킨 ‘이안길’, 단풍 내린 ‘소망이루길’… 비경 내장한 산으로
items.snippet: 전체 인구 10만531명(2026년 9월 기준)의 인구 감소 지역에 속한 소도시가 매년 단풍 절정 시기 즈음인 10월 말, 11월 초만 되면 수십 만명의 관광객으로 들썩인다. 전남광주통합특별시 장성군, 전북 순창군과 함께 내장산국립공원을 품고 있는 전북 정읍시 얘기다. 정읍시에 따르면 올해 내장산 단풍 절정 시기는 7~8일 무렵으로, 기상 이변이 없는 한 중순까지 만추의 운치를 만끽할 수 있을 것으로 예상하고 있다. 벌써 입동(立冬·11월 7일)이라고 포기 마시라. 단풍 막차에 올라탈 가을의 최전선, 내장산이 있으니.

items.title: 이혼 소장만으론 부족해? 고소장까지 내는 요즘 부부들
items.snippet: 가정법원 판사로 일한 적이 있어서인지 이혼 사건을 자주 맡는 편이다. 이혼 상담을 하다 형사법 이야기를 하는 일이 늘었다. 배우자 명의 계좌에서 1년치 생활비를 미리 빼놓으면 절도가 되는지, 배우자 휴대폰에서 증거를 채집하면 처벌되는지 묻는다. 과거에는 간통죄 고소를 빼면 이혼 소송 중에 배우자를 형사고소하는 일이 드물었다. 배우자에게 폭행을 당한 경우조차 고소를 안 하는 경우가 훨씬 많았고 고소를 해도 경찰이 수사를 꺼렸다. 흥신소를 통해 미행하며 몰래 사진을 찍거나 모텔 문을 따고 들어가는 일을 두고도 범죄라는 인식이 희미했다.

items.title: 감옥 갈 사람 2명 중 1명은 사회로 나온다
items.snippet: 지난달 13일 오후 인천 남동구의 한 상가 푸드코트에서 식사를 하던 시민 100여 명은 순식간에 지옥을 경험했다. 양손에 흉기를 묶은 최충락(59)이 식사 중이던 이들을 무차별적으로 공격했기 때문이다. 8명이 다쳤고, 중태에 빠진 한 여성은 아직 깨어나지 못하고 있는 것으로 전해졌다.

items.title: 정부 지정 ‘귀하신 몸’? 무주택자는 웁니다
items.snippet: “무주택자에게만 집을 보여주겠다는 주인이 많아요. 답답하네요.”

items.title: 백석과 국수
items.snippet: 누르스름한 표지에 그려진 시인의 아스라한 얼굴, 백석(白石)이었다. 어느 문예지를 정기 구독하면 책을 선물로 받을 수 있었는데 그때 내가 고른 게 백석 시 전집이었다. 한 편을 읽는 데 많은 공과 시간이 들었다. 낯선 평안북도 방언과 한자 탓에 사전과 옥편을 번갈아 찾아가며 발굴하듯 읽었다. 곧 절반도 못 읽고 책을 덮었다. 어려워서가 아니었다. 좋아서였다. 더 깊이 빠져들어 백석을 사랑하게 되면 나의 시를 쓰지 못할 것 같은 막연한 불안이 들었다.

items.title: 집 밖으로 나온 김장, 이색 체험이 되다
items.snippet: #1. 경기도 수원에 사는 직장인 이모(46)씨는 올해 처음 집 근처 김장 수업을 예약했다. 이씨는 “외할머니가 돌아가시고 어머니도 허리가 좋지 않으셔서 집안에서 김장하는 일이 사라졌다”며 “그동안 사서 먹기만 했는데, 우리 가족이 먹을 김치 정도는 직접 담그고 싶어 수업을 신청했다”고 했다.

items.title: 멈춤 체험 [고혜련의 삶이 있는 풍경] (28)
items.snippet: 방향을 잃고 정신없이 휩쓸리는 삶의 속도에서 비켜나 느림과 정적의 시간이 간절해질 때가 있다. 그때 은밀히 품어주는 곳이 있다. 가끔 그곳으로 간다. ‘템플스테이’ 하는 산속 사찰이다. 특정 종교인만 가는 곳이 아니다. 과도한 초(超)연결시대, 번잡한 세상사를 벗어나 홀로 자신의 꾸밈없는 본색과 마주하고픈 이들에게 살아갈 힘을 재충전해 주는 ‘피난처’ 같다.

items.title: 인간의 속도, 우주의 시간
items.snippet: 보이저 1호는 탐사선 가운데 지구로부터 가장 멀리 떨어져 있습니다. 이 보이저 1호가 오는 18일 새로운 역사를 씁니다. 1977년 발사된 지 49년 만에 지구에서 1광일(light-day·빛이 하루 동안 가는 거리) 떨어진 곳에 도달한다고 합니다. 1광일은 약 259억206만㎞입니다. 지구~태양 사이의 약 173배에 이르는 거리입니다.

items.title: 처마 밑까지 쌓인 눈에 대한 기억
불안한 실존은 占에 기대곤 했다
items.snippet: 1966년, 초등학교 1학년 여름방학 때의 일이다. 읍내에서 30리 떨어진 산골 마을에 아이스케이크 통을 실은 자전거가 나타났다. “아-이-스-께-끼-!” 소리가 들리자 아이들이 뛰쳐나갔다. 쌀이나 보리 등 농산물을 가져가면 ‘아이스께끼’로 바꿔줬다. 부모들이 논밭에 나가 있었기에 동네 ‘형아, 누나’들의 ‘절도’는 쉬웠다. 필자도 처마 밑에 말리던 마늘 한 통을 뽑아 들고 나갔다. 아까워서 조금씩 핥아먹은 것이 화근이었다. 두 살 위 둘째 누나에게 들켰다. 누나는 밭일에서 돌아온 어머니께 일러바쳤다. 어머니의 응징은 혹독했다. 당연히 저녁밥도 굶었다.

items.title: 우리에게 발라드란 무엇인가
items.snippet: “제가 음악을 할 수 있게 응원해 주시고 챙겨주신 마음들 덕분에 요즘 사랑이라는 감정을 많이 느끼고 있었는데요. 이 곡에도 그런 표현이 있더라고요. ‘나의 사랑은 함께 숨 쉬는 자유’라는 가사를 좋아하는데 꼭 특별한 걸 해주지 않아도 함께 숨 쉬면서 같이 있어 주는 게 사랑이라고 생각해요.”

items.title: “응애, 이번 생은 인도 농부래”… 인생 뽑기에 빠지다
items.snippet: 태어난 곳은 부르키나파소의 농촌 마을. 가난한 집안에서 자라 학교 대신 농장에서 일했다. 끼니를 거르는 날이 잦았고, 열다섯에 결혼해 두 아이를 낳았다. 그러나 남편의 폭력에 시달리다 이혼했다. 이후 이미 아내가 있는 남자와 재혼해 셋째 아이를 낳았다. 마흔둘에는 이웃 나라 코트디부아르로 이주했고, 손주 다섯 명을 봤다. 생의 마지막까지 농장 일꾼으로 일하다 말라리아로 세상을 떠났다. 향년 57세.

items.title: 낚시·탐조·천체 관측… ‘아재 취미’가 인기라는데
items.snippet: #1. 직장인 유모(34·강서구)씨는 요즘 주말마다 어복(魚福)을 기원한다. 그는 지난 9월 서해안 주꾸미 낚시를 다녀온 뒤 그 매력에 빠져 거의 매주 낚싯배를 타고 있다. ‘아저씨 취미’라는 시선에 망설임은 잠시, 막상 배에 올라보니 연령대가 다양했다. 유씨는 “고민 끝에 10만원짜리 낚싯대도 장만했다”며 “기다리는 시간이 지루할 줄 알았는데 오히려 그 시간을 즐기게 됐다”고 했다.

items.title: 대기업 다니던 50대 김 부장, 이제 9급 공무원입니다
items.snippet: “연금이 큰 이유였죠.” 9급 공무원 시험에 합격해 다음 주 경북도청으로 출근 예정인 김씨는 1976년생이다. 올해 쉰 살, 중소기업에 다니며 외벌이로 두 자녀를 키우던 김씨가 올해 초 ‘공시생’으로 변신하게 된 건 고용 환경 및 공무원 연금 등의 향후 안정성 때문이었다. 그는 “노안까지 온 나이에 이게 무슨 고생인가 싶었지만, 정년 연장 논의도 있고, 갈아타려면 지금이 마지막 타이밍이라고 생각했다”며 “체력 부담이 있으니 한 번에 끝내려고 바짝 집중했다”고 했다. 퇴근 후 매일 새벽 2~3시까지 집에서 인터넷 강의를 들으며 독학했다. 그렇게 도전에 나선 50대, 지난 9월 발표된 경북도 지방공무원 전체 합격자 중 23명이었다.

items.title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
items.abstract: Designing a crystal for a target property requires choosing its elements, stoichiometry, and atomic structure together, yet gradients exist only for the continuous structural variables. We introduce differentiable Equiformer fast effective-atom theory (DEFEAT), which lets a pretrained EquiformerV3 foundation model accept continuous species weights and site occupancies without retraining on fractional data, thereby enabling gradient-based materials optimization. Gradients from fine-tuned property models and a machine-learned energy penalty then guide updates to composition, atom count, atomic positions, and lattice vectors in a single optimization. items.title: High-Volume Wurtzite MnSe in MnSe/CdSe Superlattices: Structure, Magnetism and Optical Response
items.abstract: Polymorphism in Mn-based chalcogenides offers access to magnetic semiconductors with distinct crystal symmetries, polar structures, and different magnetic orders. In particular, wurtzite MnSe exhibits an appealing interplay of electric polarization and several competing magnetic phases including altermagnetic order. However, stabilizing metastable polymorphs, such as wurtzite MnSe, in experimentally useful volumes remains challenging. Here, we show that a nanoscale-period MnSe/CdSe superlattice stabilizes wurtzite MnSe over micrometer-scale total thickness while suppressing the formation of the thermodynamically favored rock-salt phase. The increased magnetic volume enables bulk-sensitive characterization of this polar polymorph. items.title: Topology as a Design Variable: Joint Architecture-Sizing Optimization for SRAM
items.abstract: SRAM's power-performance-area-stability trade-off depends on bitcell topology, a discrete architectural choice that interacts non-separably with continuous transistor sizing. However, no open-source SRAM tool treats topology as an optimizable variable. OpenRAM generates SRAM layouts but performs no optimization, while OpenYield supports high-fidelity evaluation but restricts optimization to scalar sizing of a fixed 6T cell. OpenYieldV2 closes this gap through three integrated contributions. First, a fully parameterized compiler generates complete 6T and 10T SRAM macros with peripheral circuits and replica-bitline self-timing, enabling topology comparison under identical simulation conditions. Second, a few-shot TabPFN surrogate learns topology-dependent PPA responses with limited full-macro SPICE samples. items.title: Strong phonon-coupled trion emission in Janus homobilayer
items.abstract: Janus transition metal dichalcogenides with broken mirror symmetry provide a novel platform for exploring many-body effects mediated by spin-valley-phonon interactions. Strong electron-phonon coupling demands a precise match between a strong effective dipole moment and nanometer-scale charge confinement. Here, we report thermally robust and enhanced trion emission in a symmetric bilayer WSeS with an S/S stacking configuration. The inward-pointing antiparallel built-in electric fields induce a strong electron confinement effect at the interface, driving dominant trion emission at cryogenic temperatures. Furthermore, a massive electron-phonon coupling strength (3.9) resonant with the optical phonon A_1^2 energy (51 meV) contributes to the thermal stability of this trion emission at elevated temperatures. items.title: FoundaRF: A Physics-Informed Foundation Model Framework for Radio-Frequency Passive Components
items.abstract: Designing RF/mmWave passive components is a time-consuming process that relies heavily on expert knowledge and iterative EM simulations. Although recent ML surrogate models have shown great promise in accelerating passive design, they remain task-specific and lack generalization. This paper presents FoundaRF, a foundation model framework that unifies passive layout modeling across diverse layout structures and technologies. It combines a self-supervised encoder with adaptive layout processing and physics-aware decoders to enable few-shot transfer. Experiments across four semiconductor technologies show strong generalization to unseen structures, outperforming baselines with up to a 3.3x reduction in prediction error, reducing labeled-data requirements by up to fourfold, and substantially shortening design turnaround. items.title: Deep-UV All-dielectric qBIC Metasurface for Refractive Index Sensing
items.abstract: All-dielectric metasurfaces supporting quasi-bound states in the continuum (qBICs) have emerged as powerful platforms for biosensing, yet their operation remains largely concentrated in the visible and near-infrared regimes. Extending these resonances into the deep-ultraviolet (DUV) to probe the intrinsic electronic absorption of biomolecules presents substantial material and nanofabrication challenges. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a hafnium dioxide (HfO$_{2}$) metasurface supporting DUV qBICs in the wavelength range from 225 nm to 340 nm with quality factors reaching 500. We further demonstrate its refractive index sensing capabilities through integration with a microfluidic cell and optical characterization in reflection mode. We show that the introduction of an aqueous buffer leads to a further quality factor enhancement. Achieving a sensitivity of up to approximately 60 nm/RIU...

items.title: Hybrid integration of a SESAM with a silicon nitride photonic integrated circuit
items.abstract: The realization of high-performance femtosecond lasers on photonic integrated circuits (PICs) requires robust, low-loss coupling between a saturable absorber and a photonic waveguide. In this work, we demonstrate the hybrid integration of a semiconductor saturable absorber mirror (SESAM) with a silicon nitride (SiN) PIC by micro-assembly. This micro-assembly strategy transfers the non-linear functionality of the absorber onto the PIC. We characterize the linear and non-linear performance of an unbonded SESAM and of a SESAM bonded to inverse-tapered SiN waveguides. At 1560~nm, the bonded device shows a waveguide-coupled modulation depth of 5.2\%, a maximum reflectivity of 37.2\%, and a saturation fluence of 47~\textmu J/cm$^2$. This work demonstrates that SESAMs can be integrated directly onto silicon nitride-based PIC platforms and provides a pathway towards fully integrated, self-starti...

items.title: Experimental demonstration of dual-polarization nonreciprocal thermal emission at moderate magnetic fields
items.abstract: Conventional thermal emitters obey Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which requires emissivity and absorptivity to be equal at each wavelength, angle, and polarization. This in turn places a fundamental limit on a range of radiative energy technologies as well as heat transfer. This constraint can however be overcome using magneto-optic semiconductors, which break Lorentz reciprocity under an applied magnetic field. However, in most prior experimental demonstrations, nonreciprocity has been restricted to TM polarization, since the electric field of TE-polarized light is parallel to the applied magnetic field. items.title: Asymptotic-Preserving Tensor Neural Networks for 3D High-Field Kinetic Equations with Applications to Uncertainty Quantification
items.abstract: Kinetic equations in the high-field regime describe particle transport dominated by electric-field acceleration and collisional relaxation. These equations are widely used in simulations of plasmas and semiconductor devices. Typical models include the Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) and Boltzmann--Poisson systems. Their high dimensionality and multiscale nature pose two of the major challenges to accurate and efficient numerical solution. To address these challenges, we propose an asymptotic-preserving tensor neural network (APTNN) method. Specifically, to reduce high-dimensional computational costs and memory requirements, we adopt the canonical polyadic (CP) decomposition structure of TNNs to approximate their solutions. items.title: Dark-State Coherent Control of Excitons in TMD Monolayers: A Reduced Intravalley Lindblad Framework for WSe$_2$
items.abstract: Dark-state coherence in driven three-level systems underlies electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP). Their performance depends on the coupling topology: in a ladder ($Ξ$) scheme the coherence can bypass a lossy intermediate state, whereas in a $V$ scheme it is carried by two excited states that both decay. We develop a topology-resolved Lindblad framework for driven three-level excitonic manifolds at fixed center-of-mass momentum, in which a single exciton couples to phonons, the radiation field and a dilute exciton gas. The $Ξ$ and $V$ manifolds are selected from the exciton spectrum by systematically screening optical brightness, intra-excitonic dipole strength and state compactness, making the selection reproducible and transferable to other materials. items.abstract: Gate-defined semiconductor quantum dots are promising building blocks for scalable spin-based quantum processors, however their operational properties depend on several fabrication and control parameters, such as lithographic gate layout and applied voltages. Existing device architectures have been refined through repeated fabrication and experimental testing, producing layouts that support reliable device operation. However, this process does not exhaustively explore the design space, limiting the ability to obtain qubits with targeted properties. We address these challenges by presenting a differentiable inverse co-design framework for electrostatically defined quantum dots that jointly optimises gate voltages and the gate electrode layout. items.title: Hall-Density Collapse as Direct Evidence for Percolative Conduction Onset in Monolayer MoS$_2$ Transistors
items.abstract: The origin of the apparent metal-insulator transition in two-dimensional electron systems remains debated. Using temperature-dependent transport and Hall measurements on industry-relevant MoS$_2$ monolayer FETs with amorphous HfO$_2$ dielectrics, we establish classical percolation as the underlying mechanism. We report two complementary signatures of disorder-driven conduction onset: a temperature-independent Hall-density collapse as a function of absolute gate voltage and a vanishing activation energy at a characteristic carrier density $n_{\mathrm{c}}$, identified as the percolation threshold. These findings identify dielectric-interface disorder, rather than channel quality alone, as the key parameter governing device turn-on. items.title: Energy Efficient Near-Threshold Voltage Massive MIMO Computing
items.abstract: Near-Threshold Computing (NTC) offers a substan- tial energy savings, i.e., up to 10x, for digital circuits. However, due to Process, Voltage, and Temperature (PVT) variations, low voltage operating digital processors face increased susceptibility to timing errors. This work equips conventional massive MIMO algorithms with computational error detection mechanisms, en- abling reliable operation down to near-threshold voltages. While conventional hardware based Timing Error Detection (TED) systems introduce substantial overhead, this work modifies MIMO algorithms to seamlessly integrate low overhead Algorithm Based Fault Tolerance (ABFT). items.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
items.abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. items.abstract: Semiconductor nanowire lasers are promising on-chip coherent light sources for photonic integrated circuits, but integration inevitably places them in contact with other materials, thereby changing their properties upon hybridization. In this study, we examine the photonic and electronic coupling between single ZnO nanowire lasers and TMDs. Using deterministic nanomanipulation, we first hybridized the same nanowire first with a WS$_2$ monolayer and then with a MoS$_2$ monolayer. The respective lasing threshold rises, the emission is strongly quenched at high pump power densities, and the mode envelope blueshifts. Upon hybridization with bilayer, trilayer, and bulk MoS$_2$, lasing is fully suppressed. Finite-Difference Eigenmode simulations show that the TMD absorbs part of the evanescent field. items.title: A Design Rule for Passive Reconfigurable Microwave Devices
items.abstract: Every reconfigurable microwave device places a tuning element - a varactor, a diode, transistor, microelectromechanical or phase-change switch, a ferroelectric or liquid-crystal load - inside a fixed passive network. The network can make a small change of the element produce a large change of the response, and design practice often credits it with the device's tuning capability. This paper shows that a fixed, linear, passive network cannot add to that capability. Each tuning element carries a tuning budget, a dimensionless length computed from its own impedance trajectory, and a fixed passive network can transmit that budget or lose part of it, never enlarge it. items.title: Electrostatics of Chern junctions in a magnetic field
items.abstract: Electrostatic control is central to the operation of semiconductor junctions made from conventional materials. Here, we theoretically investigate the electrostatic properties of lateral junctions between two-dimensional (2D) Chern semiconductors in a perpendicular magnetic field. The spectral asymmetry of a Chern semiconductor acts as a magnetic-field-induced effective dopant density that is dependent on the Chern number. As a consequence, two regions with different Chern numbers acquire different chemical potentials at charge neutrality, leading to a built-in potential of topological origin across the junction. Using this built-in potential as a boundary condition, we solve the 2D Poisson equation to obtain the electric potential and charge density profiles, as well as the capacitance, of Chern semiconductor junctions. items.title: NN-Based FeFET Compact Modeling for SPICE Simulation
items.abstract: Prototyping and early-stage circuit evaluation for emerging transistor technologies require fast and accurate compact models for SPICE simulations. Standard physics-based compact models, such as BSIM, offer high fidelity but demand extensive domain expertise and time-consuming equation formulation for every new physical effect, significantly slowing technology development. Neural network (NN)-based models offer a scalable alternative approach, but they rely heavily on smooth numerical solver data with explicit high-order derivative information. However, measurement data suffers from complex noise patterns, making derivative extraction challenging and complicating NN-based transistor modeling. This work presents a derivative-free NN training framework employing spectral normalization to naturally smooth derivative behavior and filter measurement noise. items.title: Atomic-Scale Phonon Engineering for Enhanced Thermal Transport in Wafer-Scale-Bonded $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC Heterostructures
items.abstract: Bonding semiconductors to substrates with high thermal conductivity is a promising way to solve the heat-dissipation problem of materials that transport heat poorly, and it avoids the lattice-matching constraints of conventional epitaxy. However, the lattice mismatch remains, leaving the two materials with mismatched phonon states, while poor interface quality scatters phonons even more. Together, these effects block phonon transport across the bonded interface and make interfacial thermal resistance a critical bottleneck, calling for careful interface engineering. items.abstract: Time-resolved infrared (TR-IR) spectroscopy reveals molecular structural changes and charge-carrier dynamics on their intrinsic timescales, in photosynthesis, catalysis and optoelectronic materials, but requires complex sources of ultrashort infrared pulses, cryogenically cooled detectors to overcome thermal background, and intense probes that can perturb the sample. To date, it has been limited to steady-state measurements. Here we demonstrate its ultrafast, time-resolved form with a picosecond visible pump pulse and a silicon detector. items.abstract: Extreme events often occur sequentially, from earthquake-tsunami cascades to successive extreme losses in financial markets. The representation is invariant to componentwise strictly increasing transformations. It preserves the identity and temporal ordering of dominant exceedances but discards their magnitudes and the identities of nondominant simultaneous exceedances. items.title: Optical Ceiling on Polaron Mobility in Disordered Molecular Semiconductors: Lessons from Eumelanin
items.abstract: Polaron hopping in disordered molecular semiconductors such as eumelanin is set by energetic disorder $σ$ and reorganization energy $λ$. We show that the reduced polaron absorption band encodes this transport problem. Its value at zero energy fixes the mean hop rate, which bounds the mobility in any dimension. For Gaussian disorder and classical vibrations its centroid is $E_\mathrm{op}=λ+(1-c)σ^2/k_BT$, its variance obeys the Hush relation, and the bound is the Marcus rate at $λ\to E_\mathrm{op}$; a 1D lower bound vanishes at $k_BT^*=(1-c)σ^2/λ$, read from optics.

items.title: Analytically Calibrated Upper L-Statistics for High-Dimensional Mean Change-Point Testing
items.abstract: This paper develops upper L-statistic methods for testing and localizing a high-dimensional mean change. At each candidate split, the proposed statistics rank the squared studentized CUSUM values across coordinates and aggregate either a fixed number or a fixed proportion of the largest entries. This construction connects max-type and sum-type procedures and provides sensitivity to a wide range of sparsity regimes. We establish asymptotic null distributions under an independent-component representation allowing weak cross-sectional dependence. The limiting laws are Poisson tangent processes for fixed ranks and Gaussian-process or Gumbel laws for proportional ranks. To improve finite-sample performance, we develop analytic calibrations for marginal variance estimation, cross-sectional dependence, extreme clustering, and skewness, and establish their first-order validity. items.abstract: As the semiconductor industry transitions to the post-Moore paradigm, wafer warpage has become a critical quality issue in advanced packaging; particularly for 3D stacking and high-bandwidth memory manufacturing where die-level deformation can affect bonding quality, interconnect reliability, and yield. However, direct high-throughput measurement of individual chip warpage remains difficult in mass-production environments, while existing wafer-level metrology systems routinely provide dense 3D shape data at the wafer scale. This paper proposes a Bezier-surface-based Gaussian Process---known as Bezier-GP---for chips-on-wafer warpage modeling. items.title: Temperature-Independent Logarithmic Current Slope in Interdiffusion-Broadened Silicon pn Junction toward Low-Power Thermometry
items.abstract: With the development of cryogenic technologies such as quantum computing, there is an increasing need for low-power cryogenic thermometers that minimize self-heating. Here, we report an anomalous temperature-independent logarithmic current slope, $d(\ln J)/dV$, in heavily doped silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$ junctions with significant dopant interdiffusion and highlight the advantages of our device as a low-power, cryogenic thermometer. Electrical characterizations from 2 to 420 K reveal that, at low forward bias, $d(\ln J)/dV$ remains nearly constant, which yields a voltage-temperature responsivity that is nearly independent of bias current. The observed transport cannot be fully understood with conventional diffusion or direct band-to-band tunneling. Instead, the results suggest the contribution of trap-assisted tunneling. These results establish interdiffusion-broadened silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$...

items.title: Polariton tweezers
items.abstract: The non-invasive, deterministic manipulation of charge carriers remains a fundamental challenge in solid-state quantum technologies. Here, we demonstrate the concept of dynamic polariton tweezers capable of trapping and transporting electrons across a two-dimensional electron system via the long-range electrostatic potential of dipolar (d-) exciton-polaritons. By driving a semiconductor microcavity with a specifically engineered, non-collinear three-beam optical pump with TE-polarization, we synthesize a macroscopic polariton lattice with hexagonal symmetry. The spatially periodic field of this d-polariton condensate acts as a reconfigurable trapping landscape for the electrons. items.title: Cage-enforced i-wave altermagnetism in boron-carbon clathrates
items.abstract: The spin splitting of an altermagnet arises from a rotation that relates its two magnetic sublattices. In known cases it is fixed by the crystal structure. Here we show that guest-host frameworks separate the two roles. In the boron-carbon clathrates $M$B$_3$C$_3$ the ordered cage removes the translation between the two guest sites and enforces cubic $i$-wave altermagnetism, with six symmetry-enforced nodal planes, for any magnetic guest in the compensated state; strain retunes the class to $d$- or $g$-wave. We demonstrate the platform with GdB$_3$C$_3$: its compensated antiferromagnetic ground state is a narrow-gap semiconductor with spin splitting of 0.19 eV at the conduction-band edge, and its weakly pinned Néel vector switches the helicity-resolved optical response on and off according to the magnetic point group. items.title: Current-Confined Formation of a Buried Ge/Si Free Surface for Defect Filtering
items.abstract: Lattice-mismatched heteroepitaxy is limited by misfit dislocations, threading defects, and residual strain generated at buried interfaces. Here, we show that current-confined electrochemistry transforms the Ge/Si heterointerface into a laterally continuous nanometric free surface while preserving the Ge epilayer. A low-doped Ge layer on a conductive p-type Si substrate redirects anodization current toward the misfit-dislocation-rich interface. Numerical modelling including charge-transfer kinetics shows that this confinement arises from hole-limited charge transfer and, together with electrochemical calibration, defines a process window that combines interfacial current confinement with controlled Si porosification. items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VII. Step kinetics
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the kinetics of attachment of new segments of the crystalline lattice (pyramids) at steps on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VI. Surface diffusion on a nonmetal-terminated surface

These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs (-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb (-1-1-1) surfaces. The mixed coverage consists of Ga adatoms in the first layer with a nonmetal atom attached above them forming a triangular-based pyramid. The pyramidal structures are stable during surface jumps involving rotations around one of the basal Ga adatoms. Thus, the diffusion proceeds via rotation (pivot) of the pair of the other basal Ga adatoms around an immobile Ga adatom moving them into new, originally empty sites. Using an energy-path determination procedure, the diffusion barriers were obtained as the difference between the init...

items.title: Cross-Domain Joint-Embedding Pretraining For Heterogeneous Industrial Time Series
items.abstract: Industrial predictive maintenance and manufacturing tasks frequently contain abundant sensor measurements, but with limited labeled data. We investigate cross-domain self-supervised pretraining using joint-embedding predictive architecture for heterogeneous industrial time series (JEPA-HITS), which learns one encoder from various domains such as battery, semiconductor chemical mechanical planarization (CMP), computer numerical control (CNC) machining, and bearing while preserving dataset-specific temporal scales. We evaluate representation reuse on regression and classification problems under reduced-label downstream training, and leave-one-domain-out (LODO) pretraining. Compared with the same architecture initialized randomly, LODO pretraining reduces RMSE from 10.72 to 7.95 on battery remaining useful life (RUL), 4.34 to 3.89 on CMP, and 13.53 to 11.72 on tool wear regression, while im...

items.title: Gate-tunable superconductor-semiconductor coupling and its impact on zero-energy modes in PbTe-Pb nanowires
items.abstract: Superconductor-semiconductor coupling in hybrid nanowires plays a pivotal role in Majorana devices. Here, we demonstrate this tunable coupling in PbTe-Pb nanowires and its impact on the induced gap and zero-bias peaks (ZBPs). In the strong coupling regime, the device reveals a clean superconducting gap, where robust and non-robust ZBPs are observed in distinct magnetic field ranges. Conversely, increasing the gate voltage drives the system toward the weak coupling regime, where the gap becomes narrow and soft. Consequently, robust ZBPs disappear while non-robust ones persist. Our results establish a direct link between tunable coupling and robust ZBPs, providing guidelines on engineering Majorana zero modes and topological qubits.

items.title: Amplification of valley polarization in an hBN-separated MoSe2-WSe2 heterostructure
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide heterostructures host long-lived interlayer excitons in the +K and -K valleys that can encode long-lived valley polarization. We investigated the low-temperature valley polarization dynamics in an MoSe2-bilayer hBN-WSe2 heterostructure. The bilayer hBN spacer results in an interlayer exciton lifetime exceeding 2 μs and an anomalous valley polarization amplification effect. Our theoretical model shows that this amplification results from the long exciton lifetime and exciton-exciton interactions. This work sets the stage for long-lived interlayer excitons to be used in nonlinear valleytronic transistors and amplifiers.

items.title: Optical Detection of Coefficient of Thermal Expansion via Frequency Tracking at Cryogenic Temperatures
items.abstract: Accurate characterization of the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) in nanoscale thin films is critical for predicting residual stress and ensuring the reliability of modern micro-electromechanical systems and advanced semiconductor architectures. The primary limitation is that traditional methods depend on precise thickness measurements or are restricted to crystalline materials. In this work, we present an in-situ, non-destructive optical methodology to determine the CTE of suspended nanofilms by tracking the temperature-dependence of their vibrational frequency. This approach eliminates thickness measurements entirely and works for amorphous films where X-ray diffraction (XRD) fails. We experimentally validate this technique across a broad temperature range, evaluating membranes in their native microstructure state without requiring additional destructive patterning or complex sam...

items.title: Band Alignment of Grafted versus Directly Bonded Si/Ge Heterostructures
items.abstract: The electronic properties of semiconductor heterostructures are influenced by the local bonding and electrostatic environment at the heterointerface. Here, we investigate how the interface-formation mechanism modifies the band alignment of Si/Ge heterostructures by directly comparing Al2O3-mediated semiconductor grafting with direct bonding. Interface-sensitive X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy combined with Kraut analysis reveals type-I band alignment for both structures, but with different band offsets: the valence-band offset increases from ~0.08 eV for directly bonded Si/Ge to ~0.21 eV for grafted Si/Al2O3/Ge, accompanied by a corresponding reduction in the conduction-band offset. Raman spectroscopy further distinguishes the two interfacial configurations. The different core-level shifts and band offsets indicate that the electronic structure is sensitive to the interfacial bonding an...

items.title: Nondestructive 3D Metrology of Through-Glass Via Geometry and Internal Wall Texture Using Holotomography
items.abstract: Through-glass vias (TGVs) are increasingly important for semiconductor packaging, yet their internal geometry and wall texture remain difficult to characterize nondestructively. Here, we use holotomography (HT) to inspect the three-dimensional (3D) geometry and internal wall texture of intact, unfilled TGVs before metallization. HT reconstructs the refractive index (RI) distribution of the glass and via. Maps of RI and spatially filtered RI then localize the internal boundary. Geometric fitting quantifies via dimensions and taper, while spatial filtering separates slowly varying wall form from finer texture. The reconstructed surface supports volumetric visualization, dimensional measurements and spatial characterization of wall texture within one optical inspection workflow. These measurements reveal internal features inaccessible from surface views and provide quantitative descriptors...

items.title: Trapping photo-carriers in undoped gate-defined quantum dots using an on-chip microwave resonator for charge readout
items.abstract: Scaling up gate-defined quantum dot systems is hindered by the rapid growth in the number of control gates. To tackle this challenge, we propose a different approach where the quantum dots are created from optically generated charges trapped beneath accumulation gates. By shining an above-the-gap laser light onto an undoped GaAs substrate, we demonstrate that it is possible to create and separate electron-hole pairs to form quantum dots. For the charge readout, we use a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator capacitively coupled to the quantum dots. With these elements, we demonstrate a working many-charge double quantum dot device comprised of only two plunger gates, one tunnel coupling gate and one sensing gate. With our approach, we show that populating quantum dots does not require engineered reservoirs, source/drain bias, ohmic contacts, or in-situ doping. As a result, the num...

items.title: Cryogenic performance of Silicon Photo-Multipliers at LN$_2$ temperature and at 3 K in the RES-NOVA cryostat
items.abstract: Silicon Photo-Multipliers (SiPMs) are semiconductor-based photodetectors that offer performance comparable to that of traditional Photo-Multiplier Tubes (PMTs), while providing several advantages, including low operating voltage, immunity to magnetic fields, compact size, and mechanical robustness. These features have led to their widespread adoption in scintillator-based detectors for both fundamental and applied physics. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in the detection of scintillation light at cryogenic temperatures in low-temperature experiments based on bolometric detectors, such as RES-NOVA and CUPID, as well as in emerging quantum applications. In the RES-NOVA experiment, radiopure PbWO$_4$ crystals are used to detect supernova neutrinos. The scintillation of PbWO$_4$ can only be evaluated at cryogenic temperatures, as the scintillation light yield is negligible...

items.title: Self-driven beta-radiation detection through a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure
items.abstract: Large-volume neutrino observatories, exemplified by IceCube, exploit Cherenkov light generated by neutrino-induced charged particles in Antarctic ice, highlighting the potential of water-based media for high-energy particle detection. In $β$-decay, a neutron converts into a proton via the weak interaction, emitting an electron and an electron antineutrino. The electron constitutes the beta radiation detected in this work, while the accompanying antineutrino motivates future extensions toward neutrino detection. Here we demonstrate a complementary electrical transduction strategy using a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure that generates reversible current transients under beta irradiation at zero applied bias. Energetic electrons deposit energy in silicon, producing nonequilibrium carriers that perturb the semiconductor surface potential and electric displacement across the adjacent a...

items.title: Energy Transfer and Strong Coupling in Plasmonic Systems
items.abstract: The coupling between plasmon resonances of metal nanostructures and electronic excitations of molecular/semiconductor systems is important in a number of applications, including surface enhanced spectroscopy, hot-electron catalysis, plasmon-induced resonance energy transfer and the creation of hybrid light-matter states. The past several decades has seen a large number of experimental studies of these effects, as well as the development of theory to explain the results. In this Perspectives article we use classical electromagnetic (EM) simulations to examine how the localized surface plasmon resonances (LSPRs) of metal nanoparticles and propagating surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) in extended metal nanostructures (wires/plates/films) are affected by interactions with a molecular/semiconductor system. The classical EM simulations are complemented by a quantum model for plasmon-exciton co...

items.title: Cross-Scale Spatial Reasoning: A Learning-Centered Framework for Designing Immersive Learning Environments
items.abstract: Understanding complex scientific and engineering systems often requires learners to connect structures, processes, and behaviors across different spatial scales and levels of organization. Although research on spatial cognition, scale, multiple representations, and systems thinking has examined aspects of this challenge, these perspectives do not always provide explicit guidance for designing learning activities that require learners to integrate information across levels. Immersive technologies offer opportunities to explore otherwise inaccessible structures, coordinate representations, and investigate system behavior, but their educational value depends on the reasoning they support. This paper proposes Cross-Scale Spatial Reasoning (CSSR) as an integrative framework for understanding how learners establish and use spatial and structural relationships across scales or organizational le...

items.title: Reasoning Across Scales: Learning Challenges and Opportunities for Immersive Technologies in Chip Design Education
items.abstract: As demand for semiconductor talent grows, education must prepare learners for the complexity of modern chip design. Instruction typically relies on lectures, textbooks, software exercises, and limited laboratory experiences. Although foundational, these approaches offer limited support for understanding the spatial, multi-scale, and interconnected nature of chip design. Virtual reality (VR) can help learners visualize and interact with complex structures and processes, but its educational opportunities remain underexplored. We examined this gap through chip design curriculum analysis and semi-structured interviews with five participants representing instructional and learner perspectives. We characterized four learning demands: descriptive knowledge, procedural knowledge, relational and design-focused reasoning, and strategic decision-making. We identified challenges in connecting abstra...

items.title: Visualizing Anisotropic Charge Transport in CrSBr using Bias-Dependent Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
items.abstract: Anisotropic semiconductors offer unique opportunities for next-generation electronics due to their direction-dependent transport. However, conventional electrical measurements provide only spatially averaged characteristics. Here, we employ bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to directly visualize the response of CrSBr under different electrical bias configurations. Spatially resolved KPFM maps reveal highly distinct, crystallographic-direction-dependent potential profiles. To elucidate this behavior, we employ anisotropic transport simulations that capture the charge transport and electric-field distributions in CrSBr. The close agreement between experiment and simulation provides a unified picture of anisotropic charge transport and bias-induced potential redistribution. Our experiments further reveal a boundary-associated redistribution of the transport field when bias...

items.title: Streaming Virtual Metrology via Lightweight Adaptation under Temporal Distribution Shifts
items.abstract: Virtual metrology (VM) aims to estimate costly or delayed metrology variables from heterogeneous sensor signals and in-line measurements, and it acts as a critical component of semiconductor manufacturing. While recent data-driven models have improved VM accuracy, most are trained in batch settings and assume stationary data distributions. In practice, however, production environments evolve continuously due to equipment degradation, process adjustments, and maintenance events, making conventional batch-trained VM models difficult to maintain under temporal distribution shifts. In this work, we propose GRAPE (Global Regression with Adaptive Prediction Enhancement), a practical online learning framework for VM in evolving wafer-processing environments. GRAPE integrates a stable global predictor based on interpretable representations with two lightweight streaming adapters that correct fea...

items.title: A Mixed-Precision CNN-LSTM Accelerator Featuring Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Dynamic Quantization for Sleep Staging
items.abstract: This letter presents a mixed-precision CNN-LSTM accelerator for EEG-based sleep staging. To efficiently execute long temporal convolutions, a serpentine dataflow propagates activations between neighboring processing elements, reducing memory accesses by 6.2 times and 2.25 times compared with output- and weight-stationary dataflows, respectively. A hybrid quantization scheme applies runtime dynamic quantization to the LSTM and MLP layers and assigns mixed precision on a layer-by-layer basis, reducing model size by 4.16 times. Combined with a bit-flexible MAC architecture and channel-grouped memory scheduling, the accelerator supports INT2/4/8/16 inference. Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS, the accelerator consumes 0.40 mW and achieves a 258 times speedup over an iso-frequency 32b RISC-V processor. items.title: Effect of Rapid Thermal Annealing on the Superconductivity of ALD-Grown TiN thin films
items.abstract: Titanium nitride (TiN) is a promising superconducting material for scalable quantum technologies owing to its tunable kinetic inductance and compatibility with CMOS thin-film processing. However, the superconducting performance of atomic-layer-deposited TiN can be degraded by oxygen incorporation, off-stoichiometry, and crystallographic disorder. In this work, we investigate rapid thermal annealing (RTA) in high-purity nitrogen as a post-deposition strategy to improve polycrystalline TiN films grown by RF-biased plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition. Grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction reveals reduced peak broadening, a smaller lattice parameter, and a stronger (111) preferred orientation with increasing annealing temperature. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling shows reduced oxygen-related bonding and a shift toward a Ti--N-dominated chemical environment after annealing....

items.title: Route-Aware EM Surrogate for Automated LC Matching Network Optimization
items.abstract: This paper proposes an open-source automated LC matching network optimization framework that combines schematic-level design optimization with electromagnetic (EM)-aware post-layout refinement. An ML-based surrogate predicts the frequency-dependent complex admittance of individual routes, enabling reuse across matching network topologies and physical layouts for the same technology node without retraining. These route models guide post-layout passive retuning to recover matching performance while preserving the layout footprint. Evaluated in a commercial 65nm CMOS technology, the surrogate achieves 1.94-4.91% mean absolute percentage error with respect to a full-wave electromagnetic solver, with no detected passivity violations. items.title: Field-resolved observation and quantification of the instantaneous Kerr response in semiconductors
items.abstract: The optical Kerr effect, whereby the refractive index of a material changes with light intensity, underpins nonlinear photonics and emerging mid-infrared technologies. Accurate determination of the nonlinear refractive index is therefore essential, yet conventional intensity-based techniques infer the nonlinear phase shift indirectly from changes in beam propagation or optical spectra. Moreover, methods such as the $z$-scan cannot resolve the temporal evolution of the nonlinear response, making it difficult to distinguish instantaneous Kerr nonlinearities from delayed contributions, including free-carrier effects. Here, we investigate the nonlinear optical response of germanium at $5 μ\mathrm{m}$ using field-resolved degenerate pump-probe spectroscopy. items.abstract: Scaling silicon spin qubits to fault-tolerant processors requires semiconductor foundry integration, yet it remains unclear how industrial fabrication and dense device integration affect qubit control and noise. items.title: Full-Potential Korringa Kohn Rostoker Study of Structural and Mechanical Properties in SiGeSn Alloys
items.abstract: Accurate first-principles descriptions of open, covalently bonded crystal structures remain challenging within conventional Korringa--Kohn--Rostoker (KKR) approaches owing to the spherical approximations commonly employed for the effective crystal potential. Here, we systematically assess the recently developed full-potential KKR (KKR-FP) implementation in the open-source MuST package and demonstrate its applicability to diamond-structured group-IV semiconductors and SiGeSn alloys. Benchmark calculations for diamond-structured Si reveal substantial limitations of the conventional muffin-tin and atomic sphere approximations, whereas KKR-FP accurately reproduces the experimental equilibrium lattice parameter and bulk modulus, yielding 5.433 and 94.9 GPa. The full-potential treatment also recovers the semiconducting character of Si. Further calculations for elemental Ge and Sn establish the...

items.title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
items.abstract: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. We further demonstrate that Fermi-sea layer polarization provides an addit...

items.title: Photonic Crystal Integrated Graphene-Silicon Schottky Diodes for Resonant Infrared Photodetection
items.abstract: Narrowband infrared (IR) photodetection has become a critical technology for the next generation of smart low-power photodetectors. In this work, we present a device based on a graphene-silicon Schottky junction with narrowband response in the short-wave IR (SWIR) regime. Integrating a photonic crystal (PhC) slab in the device enables a wavelength dependant tailoring of graphene absorption. The devices were characterized by photocurrent measurement, which was enhanced more than two orders of magnitude by the PhC integration. The sharp enhancements obtained can also be predicted by numerical simulation. This approach offers a highly scalable, tunable, CMOS-compatible architecture for narrowband IR photodetection, paving the way for next-generation, low-power IR sensors.

items.abstract: Inverse Low Gain Avalanche Diode (iLGAD) sensors developed at the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) in collaboration with the Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) have demonstrated an excellent Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and Quantum Efficiency (QE) in the soft X-ray range. items.abstract: We present a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and bonding properties of Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) compounds for potential optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications. Structural optimization reveals a systematic expansion of the equilibrium lattice parameters from S to Te. The calculated bulk moduli decrease from 83 GPa for Y2CdS4 to 68 GPa for Y2CdSe4 and 54 GPa for Y2CdTe4, indicating progressive lattice softening. Electronic band-structure calculations predict indirect band gaps of 2.42, 2.08, and 1.71 eV for Y2CdS4, Y2CdSe4, and Y2CdTe4, respectively, with further narrowing upon inclusion of spin-orbit coupling. The cases investigated include single adsorbed nonmetal atoms and full coverage, i.e. theta=1 of these surfaces. The calculated results include the stable sites and the energies of the single adsorbed atoms: located at H3 sites at low coverage and in on-top positions at high coverage for GaP, GaAs and GaSb. items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. I. Clean surface properties
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to elucidate the properties of the polar surfaces of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors, i.e., metal- and nonmetal-terminated. The systems considered were clean wurtzite gallium nitride (i.e. (0001) and (000-1) GaN surfaces), zinc blende gallium phosphide (i.e. (111) and (-1-1-1) GaP), gallium arsenide (i.e. (111) and (-1-1-1) GaAs), and (111) and (-1-1-1) GaSb surfaces. items.abstract: Colloidal semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are highly promising materials for various applications, yet photoluminescence intermittency (blinking) remains a key obstacle to their practical use. While recent advances have enabled partial or complete suppression of this effect, both the degree of suppression and the mechanism by which it occurs are often difficult to establish. In the present work we analyse the blinking suppression of single CdSe/ZnS QDs after treatment with p-phenylenediamine (PPD), recently discovered by Yang et al. We revisit the blinking mechanism in this system and show that it is governed predominantly by the trapping mechanism, rather than by Auger ionization as previously proposed. items.title: FrontierMat: Benchmarking Language Models at the Frontier of Materials R&D
items.abstract: To accelerate materials discovery, language models must be able to address problems at the research frontier. Yet textbook- and examination-derived benchmarks primarily assess established knowledge, leaving performance on frontier research problems largely untested. We introduce FrontierMat, a benchmark of 330 problems drawn from frontier academic and industrial research in fields including aerospace, semiconductors, embodied intelligence and nuclear fusion. Every problem is validated by leading experimentalists and industry experts in its field. Each problem presents a real study and asks the model to infer a withheld outcome or draw a conclusion from selected experimental evidence. Problems are annotated by functional domain, material system and the scale of the governing mechanism; 130 require cross-scale reasoning. The strongest general-purpose model scores only 53.7%, and on matched...

items.title: Unifying dynamical electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions from first principles
items.abstract: Electron-phonon interactions in materials with free carriers are dynamically screened by low-energy electronic excitations, yet first-principles calculations almost always treat this screening in the adiabatic approximation. items.title: Evaluating Structural and SAT Attack Resilience in Cryptographic Dynamic Logic Locking via Keystream Capping
items.abstract: Untrusted third-party entities throughout the semiconductor supply chain expose proprietary hardware intellectual property to reverse engineering, piracy, and overproduction. However, confining key-gates to primary outputs leaves internal combinational cones vulnerable to single-tap structural bypasses. items.title: Efficient Simulation of Gate Leakage Currents in Ultra-scaled Transistors from First Principles
items.abstract: To ensure high electrostatic integrity in ultra-scaled field-effect transistors (FETs), thin gate dielectric layers are typically needed, potentially giving rise to (strong) leakage currents. Being able to model this effect is therefore crucial. Here, we show how gate leakage currents can be computed at the ab initio level in WS$_2$-hBN FETs by extending the well-established quantum transmitting boundary method (QTBM). Two main challenges are tackled: (i) the calculation of the open boundary conditions (OBCs) for the gate contacts and (ii) the solution of the resulting sparse linear system of equations A x = b where the matrix A possesses an unstructured sparsity pattern. We demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state of the art and can be readily applied to simulate transistors with gate lengths exceeding 25 nm.

items.title: Online Open-World Wafer Defect Discovery using Hyperdimensional Computing
items.abstract: Conventional wafer defect analysis relies on offline, closed-world classifiers that fail to detect novel, unseen defect signatures emerging during continuous semiconductor manufacturing. To address this, we propose WaferHDC, an online open-world wafer defect discovery framework based on hyperdimensional computing (HDC). The memory-centric architecture of WaferHDC enables rapid anomaly detection and grouping of recurring failures into compact hypervector representations. This allows the memory space to dynamically scale with new defect modes without retraining a static classifier or archiving entire raw wafer history. WaferHDC first models normal spatial distributions, then dynamically groups recurring failures into persistent defect memory without labels or predefined class counts. It outperforms the strongest online baseline by 13.3 p.p. in adjusted Rand index and 10.5 p.p. in normalize...

items.title: Residual AM and PM Noise of Selected X-Band Amplifiers
items.abstract: In microwave systems design, amplitude modulation (AM) noise is often ignored relative to phase modulation (PM) noise. However, in high-performance applications requiring ultra-low PM noise, AM noise becomes a critical limiting factor due to AM-to-PM conversion mechanisms. Because AM noise specifications are rarely, if ever, provided for commercial microwave components, this study characterizes the residual AM and PM noise of several 10 GHz amplifiers. We present performance data for various Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor (HBT) amplifier designs and demonstrate the noise reduction achieved through power-summed configurations. For example, a discrete-die GaAs HBT amplifier achieves residual PM noise below $-160$ dBrad$^2$/Hz and AM noise of approximately $-155$ dB/Hz at a 1 kHz offset in a quad power-summed configuration. A notable finding is that the majority of amplifier designs surv...

items.title: Hierarchical Fourier Phase Projection for Local Electronic Observables
items.abstract: In this letter, we develop hierarchical Fourier phase projection (HPP) for the calculation of local electronic observables. The method couples the spatial decay of the density matrix with a hierarchy of Fourier probes, improving accuracy through refinement, and making use of all previously evaluated responses. The variation in the calculated observables during the refinement process carries information on the residual error. We use a locality-based model to estimate the error from these changes with no extra probing calculations. In particular, we demonstrate the method for electron densities and nonlocal pseudopotential forces for fixed Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians of semiconductors, metals and thermally perturbed silica. The convergence is significantly accelerated by the spatial decay of the density matrix, especially if the density matrix is short-ranged. The number of probes necessary to...

items.title: Uncertainty and Business-Aware Remaining Useful Life Estimation for Semiconductor Manufacturing
items.abstract: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimates guide maintenance in semiconductor manufacturing, where a late intervention can disrupt production but an early one discards usable equipment life. A single prediction does not express the uncertainty needed to choose between these outcomes. We combine Deep Learning (DL) sequence models with Simoultaneous Quantile Regression (SQR) to estimate RUL at selectable quantile levels, and evaluate maintenance decisions using Unexpected Breaks (UB), Unexploited Lifetime (UL), and a cost-weighted objective. On the $F_1$ fault mode of the 2018 PHM Data Challenge (PHM18) ion-milling dataset, we compare recurrent, Transformer, and State Space Models (SSM) architectures. Diagonal State Spaced (S4D) gives the strongest overall RUL accuracy across the evaluated quantiles. Varying the quantile and maintenance window exposes the trade-off between failure risk and earl...

items.title: Transport-Noise and Optical Witnesses of Electronic Multipartite Entanglement
items.abstract: Entanglement among particles distinguishes correlated quantum materials from conventional metals and semiconductors. Experimentally certifying intrinsic entanglement among interacting electrons in materials is important not only for classifying states of matter, but also for developing material-based quantum technologies. Here, we introduce a transport protocol for witnessing multipartite entanglement from the equilibrium current-noise spectrum, measured directly or reconstructed from optical conductivity. The appropriately integrated, symmetrized, and projected noise spectrum obeys an upper bound derived from microscopic model parameters. Unlike witnesses based on localized spins, our framework applies to general electronic states without requiring magnetic moments and remains invariant under single-particle basis transformations. We benchmark it in twisted bilayer graphene, twisted bil...

items.title: DACRI: Decision-Aware Causal Intervention Ranking for Critical Supply Chains
items.abstract: Detecting or attributing a supply-chain disruption is not the same as selecting the intervention that maximizes recoverable net value. We present CriticalSCM-Bench v1, a controlled synthetic benchmark with causal ground truth, paired factual/counterfactual rollouts, and an explicit net-value objective. Relative to a full-information train-selected static benchmark, LambdaMART improves median normalized net value by 5.7--16.2\%, with paired statistical support on the semiconductor and critical-material archetypes but not on digital infrastructure. On digital infrastructure, a domain-informed constant-buffer policy remains stronger, showing that greater model complexity is not uniformly justified. Across partial and delayed settings, LambdaMART retains 33--75\% of full-clamp value. Stress tests further show that intervention fidelity, timing, cost, and held-out disruptions can alter policy...

items.title: Fluctuation electrodynamics of quantum capacitance in electron bilayers
items.abstract: Capacitance provides a thermodynamic probe of interacting electrons. It characterizes the energy cost of transferring charge between conductors, which, in low-dimensional systems, is governed by exchange and correlation effects in addition to electrostatic contributions. We develop a theory of the quantum capacitance of electron double layers, semiconductor quantum wells as well as monolayer and bilayer graphene devices, focusing on the contribution generated by interlayer correlations. Within a functional-integral formulation we show that the separation-dependent part of the ground-state energy is, at the level of ring diagrams, exactly the nonretarded Lifshitz expression for the van der Waals energy of two conducting sheets, with reflection amplitudes built from the layer polarizabilities. items.title: Who Needs DRAM? We Have Fiber
items.abstract: The rising pressure on DRAM availability and contract pricing reflects generative AI's massive high-performance memory requirements. This pressure is heavily compounded by hyperscale data center expansion, which now consumes a significant portion of global DRAM output. In this work, we propose a new architecture, Fiber Memory, which reimagines the role of optical fiber in a hyperscale data center, deploying it as an active, recirculating delay-line memory for immutable data, such as large language model weights. We present a hybrid data- and pipeline-parallel optical broadcast delay-line memory architecture that accounts for fiber's physical realities. items.title: Graph-Based Kirchhoff Modeling of Non-Ohmic Electron Transport in Self-Assembled Nanonecklace Networks
items.abstract: Gold nanonecklace networks exhibit non-Ohmic current--voltage I-V characteristics with a sharp conduction threshold, making them promising for sensing and transistor-like devices. However, their conduction has been understood largely empirically, because experiments cannot see how conduction evolves inside the network. To address this, we develop a graph-based Kirchhoff modeling framework that resolves these internal processes, tracking the potential and current of every junction. Although every active element conducts linearly, the model reproduces the non-Ohmic response $I \propto (V-V_T)^ζ$. It also captures the experimentally observed effects of junction properties, network density, and voids, which lends confidence to its predicted internal states. These states show that the non-Ohmic response emerges from voltage-driven percolation. Conduction is governed by how junctions are conne...

items.title: Controllable Quantum Spin Hall Phases in Bi$_2$Te$_3$-Family van der Waals Heterobilayers
items.abstract: The tunability and control of topological edge/surface states are crucial for the development of new device applications. In this work, by combining first-principles calculations and Wannier-based tight-binding methods, we show the emergence of quantum spin Hall phases in van der Waals heterostructures formed by stacking two trivial quintuple layers from the Bi$_2$Te$_3$ family. We demonstrate the tunability of the edge states under interlayer strain and external electric field effects, suggesting the possibility of switching topological edge states on/off by external control. Additionally, the quantum spin Hall edge channels remain robust against interlayer twist, highlighting their stability against external perturbations. Our results provide a new way to create and manipulate two-dimensional topological phases in systems based on Bi$_2$Te$_3$ family, which can be valuable for practica...

items.title: Coexistence of Donor and Acceptor Hydrogen States in n-Type InN
items.abstract: Hydrogen often exhibits amphoteric behavior in semiconductors, but its role is in n-type InN remains unresolved. Wurtzite InN is a narrow-gap semiconductor with high electron mobility and is therefore attractive for high-speed electronics and optoelectronic applications. Here we use hard x-ray photoemission spectroscopy (HAXPES) to probe hydrogen-related electronic structure in as-grown and post-annealed InN thin films prepared at different grown temperatures. Post annealing, which reduces the concentration of hydrogen impurities in the films, shifts the core-level spectra toward lower binding energy, consistent with a chemical-potential shift associated with the passivation of electron carriers.
